messages.text: Hi, I messaged you the other day about the power supply. Its back down to 4.7 V. I have tried to attach a video showing this but not allowed. When I checked it just a few minutes ago, it was bouncing between 4.7V and 4.8V.

That's a failing PSU, not a connector. 4.7V sagging is under spec, and it won't hold a stable hashrate.

You're inside the RMA window, and it's PSU only, so you don't send the Bitaxe back. Fill this in and they'll send a return label and a replacement: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12t6skK21Qb8GfAdUQ9nOhJ1tVINJ60T3AIAsyhBwnYM/viewform

One thing I have to ask: has that unit ever been overclocked? Tampered or overclocked units aren't covered.
No, I ran it just like you guys sent it to me

Perfect, then it's covered. Put order Shop···· on the form and note the reading, 4.7 to 4.8V under load, that's all they need to approve a PSU swap. Processing is up to 10 days after it reaches the warehouse.

If you want a second pair of eyes while you wait, our Discord is quick: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, post there and mention JD (@nullhashrate).

Anything else on the other two units?
Yes. same thing appears to be happening with them now too. I will move them to a different area of the house.

All three at once points at the outlet, not at three dead supplies. If they share a power strip or an older circuit, the voltage sags under load and every unit reads low.

Moving them is the right test. Put each one straight into a wall socket on a different circuit, no strip, no extension lead, and see what the readings do.

What are they plugged into now?
A power strip plugged into the wall. Just those three by themselves, nothing else plugged into that strip or wall outlet.

That strip is my first suspect. Cheap strips drop voltage under a constant load like this, and three miners pulling together is enough to do it.

Take one unit, plug it straight into the wall, nothing else on that socket, and watch the voltage for ten minutes. If it sits at 5V, the strip is the problem and the PSUs are fine. If it still reads 4.7, that one's a genuine PSU fault and the RMA covers it.

Tell me what it reads?
Sitting steady at 4.8 V

Then it's not the strip. 4.8V straight off the wall on a healthy supply shouldn't happen.

Put all three on the RMA form with that reading, same link as before. They're all inside the window, and PSU-only means the miners stay with you.

I'm also passing this to JD on our side, since three at once is unusual, he may want to check the batch. The team is offline now and picks it up tomorrow at 10am ET, with the answer to your email.

Fastest route tonight is Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, mention @nullhashrate.
Handed to the team · Three PSUs failing at once on one order looks like a batch issue, needs JD's cal
That's with JD now, and the RMA form is the thing to get in tonight so the replacements start moving.
thanks. sent in that RMA.
Used the chat-interview skill

Good. That's the clock started, they'll come back with a return label, and processing runs up to 10 days once it lands.

Before you go, one thing: has this power supply trouble changed what you'd buy next, or are you still leaning toward adding more Bitaxes?
Yes. It has changed my thinking for the time being.
Fair enough. What's the part that's put you off, the hardware itself or how it was handled?
The parts themselves since all of them seemed to start acting up about the same time. However I can't say how it was handled yet as only one portion of it has been handled so far.

That's fair, and noted. Three going at once is exactly why I put it in front of JD rather than just filing it quietly.

You'll hear from the RMA side with a label, and JD picks it up from 10am ET today, his reply comes to your email. If anything stalls, come back here and I'll chase it.

Ok thanks.

Oh..I just checked the volts on all of them. They are holding steady now at about 4.8V. I'm no longer seeing it bounce back and forth between 4.7 and up.

Steady is better than bouncing, but 4.8V is still under where it should sit, so leave the RMA open. Don't cancel it on the strength of a quiet hour.

Worth noting the time it settled and what changed, if anything, and whether they're still off the strip. That detail helps JD.

If it drops back to 4.7 or a unit throws the fault again, write it down with the time and tell me here.
I cant say what time they settled down as I was sleeping. Yes, still off the strip. I dont trust putting them back on it again.

That's useful on its own: off the strip overnight and they stopped bouncing. The strip was doing part of it, even if 4.8 is still low.

Good call leaving them off it. I'd keep them straight in the wall from here regardless of how the RMA lands.

I've added that to what JD sees. He's on from 10am ET and will come back to you by email.
Hi... I havent heard anything back about returning these power supplys yet. Can you look into it for me?

I don't see a label issued on your side yet, and it's been over a week since you sent the form in. That's too long for you to be sitting with nothing, sorry.

I've put it in front of the team to chase the RMA directly. They're offline now and pick it up tomorrow at 10am ET, and the reply comes to your email.

Have the three stayed at 4.8V off the strip since, or has anything slipped?

Yes, and one has dipped as low as 4.6. I turned that one off and let it sit for a day. I then turned it back on and its sitting at 4.8 along with the other two. Sometimes I do catch them bouncing between 4.7 and 4.8.

Should I keep running them? Will it hurt the miner being at 4.8 and running it continuously?

Running at 4.8 won't damage the miner. Undervolt makes a Bitaxe reset or throw the power fault, it doesn't cook the chip, the heat damage risk comes from the other direction. So the two steady ones are fine to keep running.

The one that hit 4.6 I'd leave off until the replacement lands. That's the one dragging.

For a deeper read, JD is quickest on Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, mention @nullhashrate.
Ok thanks. How long should I wait before I contact you again if JD doesnt get back with me in that email?

Give it till end of day Friday. They pick this up at 10am ET tomorrow, so that's a full working day plus a bit of slack.

If nothing has landed by then, come straight back here and I'll push it again, you don't need to wait longer than that.

Worth checking spam too, the RMA label mail is the one that tends to land there.

Alright, Friday it is.

I check my spam every day but will make sure I do for the next few days.

Good. Friday, and if it's quiet, come back here.

Keep the two steady ones running and the 4.6 one off, that's the safest spot until the replacements turn up.

Thanks for the patience on this one, you've done everything right from your end.
